description: Quality rubric for AI primitives. Criteria come from the AI Primitives Hub author guides and the security scanner's rule catalogue; each criterion lists its sources.

anchors.5: Exemplary: fully meets the criterion; nothing to improve.
anchors.4: Good: meets the criterion with minor gaps.
anchors.3: Adequate: partly meets it; clear improvements needed.
anchors.2: Weak: important gaps or a real risk.
anchors.1: Failing: missing, or contradicts the criterion.

criteria.name: Purpose and scope
criteria.look_for: States one clear purpose and when to use it. A skill or prompt focuses on a single capability (single responsibility). The role and scope are explicit, and the content stays within what the description promises.

criteria.name: Structure and metadata
criteria.look_for: Follows the structure for its type: a title and headed sections; agents have Expertise, Behavior and Limitations; skills have YAML frontmatter with name and description (and ideally metadata.version, license, author). File and skill names are descriptive and kebab-case (task-name.prompt.md, role-name.agent.md, capability-name/SKILL.md).

criteria.name: Clarity of instructions
criteria.look_for: Instructions are concrete, actionable and unambiguous, with no contradictions. The primitive never tries to override other instructions or hide what it does (no directive-precedence or stealth directives).

criteria.name: Examples, edge cases and limitations
criteria.look_for: Provides clear examples or usage steps, covers edge cases, and documents limitations (what it will not do, when not to use it).

criteria.name: Least privilege and tools
criteria.look_for: Requests only the tools it needs (allowed-tools is a short explicit list, never a wildcard). No blanket permissions, permission-bypass flags, high-privilege MCP servers, unpinned or auto-approved MCP packages, or unrestricted root/home paths.

criteria.name: Safe execution and human control
criteria.look_for: Destructive or irreversible actions require explicit human confirmation. No remote scripts piped to a shell, persistence, unbounded autonomous loops or delegation, unexpected code execution, unsafe deserialization, or host network exposure.
sources: docs/reference/security-rules.md#skills-and-other-agentic-patterns (SKL-001, SKL-005, SKL-006, LLM-004, LLM-005, LLM-008, ASI-*)

criteria.name: Untrusted input and data protection
criteria.look_for: Treats user input, files and tool output as untrusted data with a stated trust boundary. Contains no prompt-injection text, hidden or encoded content, unsafe HTML, secrets or credentials, or instructions to send data elsewhere. Model output is not executed or rendered unsanitized.
